en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Muhammad Bin Al Rayyan who said,

‘Al-Mamoun cajoled Upon Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> (9<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) with every ploy but he was not enabled upon anything with regards to it. So when he was frustrated and intended to marry his daughter to him<sup>asws</sup>, sent two hundred bridesmaids from the most beautiful as could happen to be, a bowl for each one of them wherein was a jewel, to welcome Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>.

When he<sup>asws</sup> was seated in a choicest place, he<sup>asws</sup> did not turn towards them, and there was a man called Mukhariq, owner of the (good) voice, and a lute, and beat, of a long beard. So Al-Mamoun called him over, and he said, ‘O commander of the faithful! If it was regarding anything from the affairs of the world, so I shall suffice you of his<sup>asws</sup> matter’. So he sat in front of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>.

Mukhariq inhaled with an inhalation (to sing) and the people of the house gathered, and he went on to strike on his lute and sing. So when he had done so for a while and when Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> did not turn towards him, neither right nor left, then he<sup>asws</sup> raised his<sup>asws</sup> head and said: ‘Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, O one with the goatee (beard)!’. So the drum fell from his hand and the lute. So he did not benefit by his hands until (up to the day) he died.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So Al-Mamoun asked about his sate. He said, ‘When Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> shouted at me, I panicked with such a panic, I shall not be coming out from it, ever!’.
